system.name: PaymentGuard Real-Time Fraud Scorer
system.intended_purpose: Score card-present and card-not-present transactions in real time to recommend approve / step-up / decline actions to the issuer's authorization engine.
system.deployment_context: GPU inference behind the authorization gateway; <50ms p99 budget; processes ~2,400 transactions/second at peak.

governance.owner: Head of Financial Crime Analytics, Meridian Payments
governance.oversight: Step-up and decline recommendations are advisory; a rules layer and a fraud-ops analyst can override before the issuer acts on high-value transactions.

out_of_scope: Account closure or law-enforcement reporting without human review
Use as the sole basis for denying access to essential payment services
risks: False declines disproportionately affecting thin-credit-history customers
Concept drift during fraud-pattern shifts (e.g., new BIN-attack campaigns)
Adversarial probing to learn the decision boundary

measure.test_data: Time-split holdout of 12M labelled transactions from 2026-Q1, with chargeback-confirmed fraud labels and a 60-day maturation window.
measure.fairness: False-decline rate audited across issuer geography and card tier; max disparity 1.4 percentage points, reviewed quarterly by the model-risk committee.
limitations: Labels mature with a lag, so very recent fraud campaigns are under-represented
Not tuned for crypto on-ramp transactions

mitigations: Reason codes attached to every decline for dispute handling
Automatic fallback to rules layer if feature freshness degrades
manage.monitoring: Hourly score-distribution and PSI drift monitoring with paging alerts; weekly false-decline review against confirmed-fraud labels.
